headline: Oil surges 6.7% as Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate amid regional security concerns
bottomLine: Brent crude surged 6.7% to $127.61 as Strait of Hormuz tensions dominated headlines, with Iran implementing toll-booth controls while Saudi Arabia reported pipeline attacks affecting output. Egypt's currency weakened 2.3% against persistent 28.3% inflation, contrasting sharply with Gulf states maintaining low inflation below 1.5%. Qatar's robust 17.3% current account surplus underscores regional divergence as oil exporters benefit from elevated prices while import-dependent economies face mounting pressures.
notableFlows: Gulf sovereign wealth funds accelerated energy transition investments, with Qatar Investment Authority committing $12B to European renewable infrastructure amid oil price volatility.
Egyptian pound depreciation triggered $2.8B in portfolio outflows as foreign investors reduced exposure to local currency bonds despite IMF program progress.
UAE banking sector attracted $4.2B in cross-border deposits from regional institutions seeking stable currency exposure amid geopolitical tensions.
Morocco's manufacturing exports to Europe increased 18% year-over-year, benefiting from supply chain diversification and competitive labor costs.

risks.title: Strait of Hormuz Disruption
risks.description: Iran's toll-booth operations and Saudi pipeline attacks signal escalating energy chokepoint risks. With Brent crude already at $127.61, further disruptions could trigger supply shocks affecting 20% of global oil transit. Regional economies face divergent impacts based on energy export dependency.

risks.title: Egyptian Currency Instability
risks.description: The Egyptian pound's 2.3% weekly decline amid 28.3% inflation creates mounting pressure on import-dependent sectors. Foreign currency reserves remain under stress despite IMF support, with potential spillover effects on regional trade financing.

risks.title: Youth Unemployment Divergence
risks.description: Morocco and Egypt face youth unemployment above 18%, contrasting sharply with Gulf states below 7%. This demographic pressure could fuel social tensions and migration flows, particularly if regional economic growth fails to generate sufficient job creation.
